title: General World Model Control Grammar
summary: Treat video prompting as directing a simulated world rather than describing a static frame.
guidance: Name the subject, physical state, motion cause, environment, camera intent, light behavior, and emotional pressure.

title: Four-Step Prompt Method
summary: A complete cinematic prompt covers setting, action, camera, and tone.
guidance: Specify where and when the scene occurs, who or what moves, how the camera observes it, and what the viewer should feel.

title: Camera Intent
summary: The model needs camera intent, not only subject description.
guidance: Specify shot size, angle, trajectory, speed, focal feeling, and the emotional reason for the camera distance.

title: Lighting and Material Behavior
summary: Light words guide mood, surface response, and visual realism.
guidance: Describe the light source, temperature, contrast, reflections, shadows, and how materials react as motion unfolds.

title: Temporal Rhythm
summary: Video prompts should define the moment-by-moment rhythm of change.
guidance: Structure the clip with an opening beat, motion or transformation beat, lingering beat, and final visual state.

title: Reference Continuity
summary: References should anchor identity, style, motion, scene structure, or timing.
guidance: State what must be preserved from the reference and what may change. For edits, name only the delta and keep everything else stable.

title: Physical Causality and Motion
summary: Motion is stronger when the prompt explains cause, direction, speed, and consequence.
guidance: Write verbs as physical instructions: what initiates movement, where it travels, how fast it changes, and what visible consequence remains.

title: Conflict Control
summary: Too many references, broad edit prompts, or vague motion can cause unwanted changes.
guidance: Use fewer controlling ideas, assign each reference a clear role, and avoid contradictory style, camera, timing, or subject instructions.
